parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile federal layer with a state layer that is restrictive on documents but not yet on facilities. Universal or near-universal exposures: visa/entry adjudication directing refusal where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex, with a possible fraud-based lifetime bar; X markers eliminated and M/F-only issuance; exclusion from federally funded single-sex facilities; documented severe abuse (beatings, solitary, sexual abuse) for trans people in immigration custody, plus federal prison conversion-therapy policies. The state bans licence marker changes and denies birth-certificate changes, but as of April 2026 imposes no restroom restriction, its facility bill is not law, and its hate-crime aggravator applies. No criminalisation of trans identity, no execution pathway; federal courts have enjoined several measures. A trans minor cannot obtain transition care here.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 foreign-ministry cable instructs refusal where document/record discrepancy casts reasonable doubt on sex, and consideration of fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; X markers barred for new issues; eight-plus governments issued travel advisories; trans travellers report passports blocked/confiscated abroad.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, with limited waivers; suit pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ maintains guidance; existing X passports valid to expiry.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at application → refusal or investigation → possible detention; state licence/birth-certificate bans remove any route to making documents match presentation, feeding directly into federal screening doubt.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented abuse of transgender detainees in immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse, guards invoking trans status. Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for trans inmates (hair, hormone removal) from 2026; reporting on trans prisoners ceased 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No criminalisation of trans identity or expression; custody abuse documented but no statutory basis found for visitor detention on identity alone; litigation and oversight exist in principle.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or fraud inquiry can escalate a visitor into the immigration-custody system where the documented abuse occurs; state prison placement-by-birth-sex bill passed one chamber but is not law.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity — a universal exposure in federal buildings, parks and federally funded settings. State has no facility restriction as of April 2026; its 2026 facility bill died without lower-chamber hearing, though 4 nationally flagged states criminalise use and 9+ ban it in all government buildings.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State law places no restriction on restroom use matching gender identity; two cities affirmatively protect it; proposals criminalising use died in committee since 2021; 2023 appellate injunction barred schools restricting a trans student's use.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The federal facility bar applies inside this state regardless of its protective posture; the pending state bill plus a national risk assessment citing 'bathroom-ban escalation' signals movement toward a stricter state layer.

care_services.exposure: State bans all transition care for under-18s (upheld Nov 2024): a trans minor visitor cannot obtain surgery, blockers or hormones here. Federal October 2025 rule would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; specialised LGBTQ youth crisis services shut nationally in July 2025.
care_services.protection: Adult care availability in the state is not documented either way; hate-crime law and federal employment ruling do not reach care.
care_services.interaction: A family travelling with a trans minor faces denial of routine transition care, and the federal subpoena pattern (20+ hospitals' under-19 records) raises data-exposure concerns for any minor seeking care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders frame gender-affirming care as 'mutilation,' direct law-enforcement investigation of 'gender ideology' in schools, and a May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups 'radically pro-transgender'; a 2025 poll shows 66% supporting sex-at-birth markers on documents. Rewards language targets violence, not ideology, but the framing is officially hostile.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism document states powers will not target mere disagreement; cash-reward criterion excludes 'radical gender ideology'; several orders blocked or enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-level enforcement is comparatively restrained (no restroom crime, hate-crime aggravator since 2019), so federal threat-framing is the operative hostility a visitor meets at borders and federal settings.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minor denied all transition care under state law (2023, upheld 2024). Federal order directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; a state law requires schools to notify parents when a minor asks for a different name/pronoun; 2023 law bars state funds for reassignment surgery for incarcerated patients.
minors_guardians.protection: Facility restrictions in schools are not state law; 2023 school bathroom injunction stands; parent-notify law applies to enrolled students, not short-stay visitors.
minors_guardians.interaction: For a travelling family, care denial plus potential school/facility queries mean a visiting trans child is materially more exposed than a travelling adult; the guardian is not the defendant but loses care access.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2023 legislative count: 190+ anti-trans bills introduced nationally; national travel guide advises checking recent violence reports; only 23 states cover gender identity in bias statutes; this state's coverage is an aggravator only, with no charging-enforcement data.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime aggravating circumstance since 2019 covering gender identity; national hate-crime statute; national crime data show bias incidents are a minority of reported hate crime; no documented pattern of trans-specific killings in the dossier.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No denominator or trans-specific killing rate is provided, so violence is treated as background-level rather than a campaign; recourse exists but its use for gender identity is undocumented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Pending challenges (passport suit, motor-vehicle marker ban suit, health rules) mean exposure shifts by litigation timing; no enforcement data on the hate-crime aggravator; religious-freence statute's coverage of gender identity unresolved; adult care availability unstated.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Federal courts have enjoined or blocked several orders; a 2023 appellate injunction protects school facility use; legal-aid FAQ and civil-liberties litigation show functioning advocacy; employment discrimination prohibited nationally on gender identity.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Rule of law partially operates FOR trans people here (injunctions, pending suits), unlike pure hostile-state anchors, but it does not undo the operative federal document and facility rules already in force.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this dossier: Ostravia has birth-sex prison placement operative, an enacted cross-dressing crime, slow remedies and discouraged reporting. Here prison placement-by-birth-sex is only a bill that died in committee, no expression offence exists at state level, and federal courts grant real injunctions, so the score sits well above that anchor.

Higher than this anchor: Vellandra imposes a blanket, routinely enforced entry bar on transgender visitors with appeals decided by the same agency. Here entry refusal is conditional on document discrepancy, requires a four-element fraud finding that is never automatic, and is actively challenged in court — but the anchor's pure administrative exclusion is close to the entry axis here, so the gap is modest, not a tier.

Lower than this anchor: Kestrel Isles' exposure is discretionary secondary screening and administrative refusal with slow appeals. This jurisdiction adds a mandatory federal facility-exclusion rule, documented immigration-detention abuse (beatings, solitary, sexual abuse), conversion-therapy-style federal prison policy, and a state licence-marker ban — heavier universal and custody exposures than screening friction alone.

Materially lower than this anchor: Meridia has trained border officers, document acceptance matching presentation, tribunal remedies with compensation, and detention that ends in release. Here documents cannot be corrected to match, entry officers are told to refuse on discrepancy, custody carries documented abuse, and federally funded facilities are closed to trans users — none of which exists at 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one combined system. The state layer is comparatively permissive on expression — no restroom restriction as of April 2026, a hate-crime aggravator, protective city ordinances — but has closed the document route (licence and birth-certificate marker changes barred), which removes the only way an outed local or long-stay visitor could align papers with presentation. That state gap feeds directly into the federal layer, where entry adjudication treats any discrepancy as grounds for refusal and possible fraud-based lifetime inbarment, where X markers are gone, where federally funded single-sex facilities are shut, and where trans people in immigration custody have documented beatings, solitary and sexual abuse. Litigation is genuinely functioning (multiple injunctions, pending suits), which keeps this above the 0.35 anchor tier, but it mitigates rather than reverses the operative rules. For a family, the state's upheld under-18 care ban is an additional concrete denial. No criminalisation of identity and no execution pathway anchor the floor; universal document and facility exposures plus custody abuse pull it below the 0.55 screening-friction tier.
